source_text: ὑπεροχῇ τὰ αὐτοῦ. «Τίς γὰρ ὁμοιωθήσεται τῷ Θεῷ ἐν υἱοῖς Θεοῦ;» καθ' ἡμᾶς γὰρ ὁμοῦ καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑπεροχῇ θεότητος, εἰ καὶ γέγονε σάρξ. Δύο γε μὴν αἱ δαμάλεις, εἰς τύπον, οἶμαί που, τῶν δύο λαῶν, συνδεδραμηκότων εἰς ἕνα τὸν ἀπ' ἀ

pass_b_english: Cyril: …superiority are his things. ‘For who will be likened to God among sons of God?’ (Psalm 89:6) for according to us together and beyond us is Christ in superiority of godhead, even if he has become flesh. And two at least are the heifers, unto a type, I think somehow, of the two peoples, having run together unto one the from both, the one for us and with us joining unto the spiritual unity through faith. And rams again and lambs equal-numbered, and he-goats not less, hinting the multitude of those believing, the as in a fifth, I say, time having been brought together, according to which the sojourn of the one saying, ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will drag all toward myself.’ (John 12:32) And of those who have believed is signified through the rams the as in prudence perfect, and of the intelligible age—clear that the in Christ—the freshly holding, and through the lambs the as in simplicity and without-evil; ‘Do not,’ he says, ‘brothers, become children in the minds, but in the evil be infant, and in the minds become perfect’ (1 Corinthians 14:20); and through the he-goats for sin, the always needing cleansing and release of faults. Therefore also we have been taught to say in prayers: ‘Release for us the trespasses.’ (Matthew 6:12) For there is not a time, when it is not necessary to cry for those truly fresh-minded, and knowing the weak of the human nature, and, ‘Who will understand faults?’ (Psalm 19:12) and, ‘From my hidden things cleanse me.’ This is a spiritual sacrifice, also concerning salvation of our souls fragrant to God.

Cyril: So then I said Christ, as at least in the calf and in the rams, lambs and he-goats, and in the others to be signified, and I would think the word upon this not somehow to miss the fitting. And if someone should choose also to transfer the power of the thoughts upon us ourselves, nothing grieving, to bring upon the things set forth some such contemplation.
Palladius: What sort then do you say?

Cyril: The sacred victims were being brought forward according to the law from all Israel. And the blood of the things being slaughtered was being poured toward the divine altar, all but writing as in a shadow of the thing done, and sideways hinting for us, that we must dedicate our own souls to the holy God.
Cyril: So then instead of us and for us are the victims, and we are in them the ones being sacred-worked according to type.

Cyril: Come then examining uprightly the things as brought forward from all through the hand of the leaders, let us look around at the beauty of the contemplation in spirit.
